knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Oil and heated parts stay hot for a long time. The site contact confirms the appliance is off and cool before cleaning starts.
Water on hot oil or a fryer fire can spread the fire. The site fire procedure governs, and fire protection is not disturbed.
Opening slowly and to one side lets steam clear before the worker reaches in.
Oil holds heat for longer, so a surface can look cool while the oil underneath is still hot.
Rapid temperature change can crack hot oven glass. The glass is left to cool before a damp cloth is used.

practicalCriteria: Checks each surface is cool enough to touch by a method the site sets, before handling it
Uses rated heat-resistant gloves and checks them before use
Opens a hot oven or dishwasher door slowly and to one side
Describes the fire response: no water on oil or a fryer fire, and the site fire procedure followed
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate: an assessor observes the practical criteria and records the result. A knowledge pass is not practical competence and does not grant any licence or authority.
evidenceRequired: Surface check record or the reason the appliance was left until cool
Fire response details for the site
Burn, splash or steam incident record where it occurred
stopWorkCriteria: Any attempt to clean a hot surface or hot oil
Any use of water on hot oil or a fryer fire
Any disturbance of fire suppression nozzles
